acute_stroke_fast.title: Acute Stroke FAST Emergency Protocol
criteria: F - Face Drooping: One side of the face is numb or droops when smiling
A - Arm Weakness: One arm drifts downward when both arms are raised
S - Speech Difficulty: Slurred words, unable to speak, or difficulty understanding
T - Time to Call 112: Note the 'last known well' time and call immediately
acute_stroke_fast.clinical_guidance: Do NOT give aspirin, water, or food at home. Permissive hypertension is maintained to preserve brain penumbra. Transfer directly to a primary stroke center capable of 24x7 non-contrast CT, IV thrombolysis, and mechanical thrombectomy.

thunderclap_headache.title: Sudden Severe Thunderclap Headache Protocol
thunderclap_headache.urgency: CRITICAL EMERGENCY - Rule out Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
criteria: Headache reaching 10/10 maximum peak severity within < 1 minute ('worst headache of life')
Neck stiffness (inability to touch chin to chest)
Accompanying vomiting, confusion, or transient loss of consciousness
thunderclap_headache.clinical_guidance: Immediate Non-contrast Brain CT. If CT is normal and headache began > 6 hours prior, Lumbar Puncture is mandatory to check for xanthochromia. Ruptured berry aneurysm has 50% mortality if rebleeding occurs.

status_epilepticus.title: Prolonged Seizure / Status Epilepticus Protocol
criteria: Any continuous convulsive seizure lasting >= 5 minutes
Two or more discrete seizures without regaining baseline consciousness in between
status_epilepticus.clinical_guidance: Protect airway, turn patient to recovery position. Do NOT insert anything into mouth. Administer rescue benzodiazepine (IV Lorazepam 4 mg or IM Midazolam 10 mg). Escalation to second-line IV Levetiracetam/Fosphenytoin if seizure continues past 10 minutes.

bacterial_meningitis.title: Acute Bacterial Meningitis Triage Protocol
bacterial_meningitis.action: Immediate Emergency Department isolation and treatment
criteria: Triad of: High Fever + Nuchal Rigidity (stiff neck) + Altered Mental Status
Purpuric or petechial non-blanching skin rash (meningococcal disease)
bacterial_meningitis.clinical_guidance: Do NOT delay antibiotics for lumbar puncture or neuroimaging. Draw blood cultures and immediately administer IV Ceftriaxone 2 g + Vancomycin + Dexamethasone 10 mg.

mental_health_crisis.title: Mental Health Crisis & Suicide Prevention Protocol
mental_health_crisis.action: Connect immediately to 24x7 verified crisis counselors

helplines.name: Tele-MANAS (Govt of India)
helplines.details: Toll-free 24x7 mental health service in 20+ Indian languages

helplines.name: KIRAN Mental Health Helpline
helplines.details: Ministry of Social Justice, 24x7 psychological support

mental_health_crisis.clinical_guidance: Do NOT attempt to diagnose psychiatric conditions from chat messages. Express calm empathy, validate distress, ask directly if the person is safe right now, remove immediate means of harm, and facilitate immediate warm handover to professional crisis counselors or a trusted family member.
